title: Essen und Trinken — die ersten Bilder

blocks.title: Guten Appetit! — two tables, one lesson

paragraphs.text: The red band across the top of the page is the promise of the whole chapter: plan a shopping trip, talk at the shop counter, talk at the table, say what you like to eat, and learn a strategy for ordering words so they stick. Everything below it is the first step — the food itself.

Two photographs divide the page into the two meals you already know. The first table is set for {{de:Frühstück}}, the second for {{de:Mittagessen}}. Learn the words inside the meal they belong to: a word that arrives with a picture of a breakfast table is far harder to lose than a word in an alphabetical list.
Frühstück: die Banane · der Orangensaft · das Müsli · der Joghurt · der Tee · die Milch · der Käse · die Marmelade · das Ei · das Brötchen

Notice that every noun is printed with its little helper word in front — {{de:die}}, {{de:der}} or {{de:das}}. Say it aloud that way from the start: the article is not decoration, it is half of the word, and later this lesson it will decide the shape of the whole sentence.
Mittagessen: der Apfelsaft · die Kartoffeln · das Salz · der Pfeffer · das Gemüse · das Wasser · der Essig · das Öl · die Cola · das Fleisch

In exercise 1b you are asked which words sound similar in your own language. Food is the friendliest area for this trick — the page itself gives one away: {{de:„Banane" heißt auf Russisch „banan"}}. Keep a corner of your notebook for these near-identical words; they cost you almost nothing to learn.
